replies.text:
Step 2 checks:

- Automated abuse of reachable endpoints: design says "Customers chat with an AI support agent in the public mobile app" — present; covered by listed threat 6 (bot flooding of chat/LLM cost) and listed threat 4 (scraping of order data). No sign-in or sign-up exists ("auth": false, nothing in design text), so brute force / mass sign-up / email-SMS flooding do not apply.
- Staff, admin, moderator or support screens showing user-supplied content: the design describes only "Customers chat with an AI support agent in the public mobile app" — no human staff or admin console is stated. Not applicable.
- Money moved / approved with no record of who did it: "The agent can issue refunds up to $200 through the Stripe payment API" — present; already covered by listed threat 9 (agent-issued refunds cannot be traced).
- Personal or financial pages cacheable by browsers, proxies or CDNs: design states only a chat in a "public mobile app" with tool lookups; no page, document or download delivery is described. Not applicable.
- Attacker-controlled text reaching logs, CSV/spreadsheet exports, emails or headers: attacker-supplied order fields exist ("order history, which contains email addresses and shipping address") but the design names no log, export, email or downstream interpreter; the context-poisoning path is already listed threat 5. Not applicable as a separate threat.
- Single-reviewer items: ownership scoping on order id is the same attack as listed threat 2 ("claim to be a customer by stating an order number or email, and reach both the order history lookup and the Stripe refund"); the prompt-only $200 cap is listed threat 3; LLM-provider PII minimisation is listed threats 8 and 4. All covered.
